destination.name: Macarthur
destination.tagline: Sydney's south-west edge, where the colonial wool estate around Camden meets suburbs and bush.
destination.description: Macarthur is a region on the outer south-west of Greater Sydney covering Campbelltown City, Camden and Wollondilly Shire, about 3,067 square kilometres. It is named after John and Elizabeth Macarthur, pioneers of the Australian wool industry, whose Camden Park grant began with 5,000 acres in 1803. Visitors come for Camden's and Picton's heritage streets, Campbelltown's free arts centre and Thirlmere Lakes National Park, five freshwater lakes in the Greater Blue Mountains World Heritage Area.
whyVisit: See Picton’s Victoria Bridge and tunnel

goodToKnow.title: Thirlmere track
goodToKnow.detail: The 6 km Thirlmere Lakes walk starts at Couridjah picnic area and has no directional signage, though the track is well defined.

goodToKnow.title: Closures
goodToKnow.detail: Lake Couridjah picnic area is closed until 30 November 2026, and there is no swimming or canoeing in the lakes when water levels are low.

goodToKnow.title: Spread out
goodToKnow.detail: The three councils cover over 3,000 sq km, so a car is the practical way to link Camden, Picton and Campbelltown.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} suit the walks at Thirlmere Lakes and Picton, and spring is the time to see the park's ground orchids.
